summary: Phenazopyridine is an azo dye that exerts a local analgesic effect on the mucosa of the urinary tract, relieving the pain, burning, urgency and frequency caused by lower urinary tract irritation from infection, trauma, surgery or instrumentation. It is NOT an antibiotic and treats only symptoms. When used with an antibacterial agent for a UTI, it should not be given for more than 2 days. It turns urine reddish-orange and can cause methemoglobinemia and hemolytic anemia, especially in G6PD deficiency or renal impairment.
indications: Symptomatic relief of pain, burning, urgency, frequency and other discomfort arising from irritation of the lower urinary tract mucosa caused by infection, trauma, surgery, endoscopic procedures, or passage of sounds or catheters

moa: Phenazopyridine hydrochloride is excreted in the urine, where it exerts a topical (local) analgesic effect on the mucosa of the urinary tract, relieving burning, pain, urgency and frequency. The precise mechanism of action is not known.

absolute: Severe hepatitis or severe liver disease
relative: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency - increased risk of hemolysis
monitor: Patients at risk of methemoglobinemia or hemolytic anemia
Patients in whom the underlying cause has not been treated

preg: Pregnancy Category B. Reproduction studies in rats at doses up to 50 mg/kg/day showed no evidence of impaired fertility or fetal harm; however, there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if clearly needed.
lact: There is no information on whether phenazopyridine or its metabolites are present in human milk. Use with caution in nursing mothers.
renal: Contraindicated in renal insufficiency. Giving usual doses to patients with impaired renal function may lead to increased serum levels and toxic reactions. A yellowish tinge of the skin or sclera may indicate accumulation due to impaired renal excretion and the need to discontinue therapy.
hepatic: Contraindicated in severe hepatitis and severe liver disease. Renal and hepatic toxicity have been reported, usually at overdose levels.

moderate: Other oxidant drugs - additive risk of methemoglobinemia/hemolysis, especially in G6PD-deficient patients
interactions.food: Take after meals to minimize gastrointestinal upset.
interactions.alcohol: No specific alcohol interaction described in labeling.
interactions.diagnostics: As an azo dye, phenazopyridine colors the urine and may interfere with urinalysis and colorimetric/spectrometric laboratory tests (e.g., color-based tests for glucose, ketones and bilirubin).

missed: No specific missed-dose instruction is provided in the labeling. General guidance: take the missed dose when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it; do not double the dose. Because therapy is usually short (often <=2 days), simply resume the regular schedule.
overdose: Overdose, or usual doses in renal impairment, may cause methemoglobinemia, oxidative (Heinz-body) hemolytic anemia, and renal or hepatic impairment. Methemoglobinemia is treated with methylene blue 1 to 2 mg/kg IV or ascorbic acid 100 to 200 mg orally, which should cause prompt reduction. Provide supportive care.
